sections.h2: Three ways to sell a Marietta house
sections.html:
Your options in Marietta: hire an agent, handle the sale yourself, or accept a cash offer. Repairs and timing usually point to one of them.

Hiring an agent brings in mortgage buyers, and with them showings, inspection requests and a closing date that follows the lender. Doing it yourself saves the agent's share but hands you pricing, marketing and negotiation. A cash buyer closes sooner and asks for no repair list, but the price reflects the house as it stands today.

Typical home values here are $448,500, so a small percentage gap between two offers is a big gap in cash. Compare terms in writing before you decide, and ask each buyer who pays closing costs and when funds arrive.

About 63,574 people live in Marietta today by the 2025 estimate, up 4.1% from the 61,060 used as the 2020 starting point. Renters fill just over half the homes, since owners occupy 47.2%. Owner costs are $2,170 a month with a mortgage and $618 without. Gross rent is $1,586. The city has 24,707 households averaging 2.40 people.

Owners of older houses near the Square should ask the city which exterior changes need approval in the historic district before promising a buyer any work. Code Enforcement covers that district along with zoning and signs.

The City of Marietta enforces the 2024 editions of the International Building Code and International Residential Code, with 2026 Georgia amendments, for projects permitted after January 1, 2026. Plumbing, mechanical and fuel gas codes follow the 2024 editions as well, and the electrical code is the 2023 National Electrical Code with 2026 Georgia amendments.

All building permits are submitted online. Pulling a permit before repairs matters at sale time, because a buyer's inspector or title review may turn up unpermitted work. The Building Inspection Division answers questions at 770-794-5659.

Code Enforcement checks building code, zoning, signs, the historic district and the standard housing code. It sits at 205 Lawrence Street, phone 770-794-5439, and it can act only on properties inside the city limits. A Marietta mailing address does not guarantee the house is inside the city, so use the city's Property Search Tool to confirm which rules apply.

sections.h2: Cobb County property tax and Marietta's city bill
sections.html:
County and school taxes both come on a bill from Cobb's Tax Commissioner. The seven cities inside Cobb, Marietta among them, run their own billing, so ask the City of Marietta about its separate portion.

Cobb tax year milestones
StepRule
Assessment dateEach January 1 sets who owes for the year
Personal property returnsDue at the Tax Assessor's office by April 1
Bills mailedBy August 15
Payment dueOn or before October 15
Late payment5% penalty plus monthly interest

The county does not split the bill between seller and buyer. Who owes what is set by the closing paperwork, and the purchaser generally takes on the liability. The tax is figured for the full year and follows the property.

Partial payments are fine, and a postmark from the U.S. Post Office dated by midnight on the deadline counts as on time. Metered or kiosk postage does not count. An owner appealing a value must still pay at least the appeal amount by the due date. Pay at 736 Whitlock Avenue, Suite 100, Marietta, or by mail to PO Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061. The office phone is 770-528-8600. Bills for 2026 also carry the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant, which is separate from homestead exemptions.

Drop boxes sit outside the Whitlock Avenue office, and the East Cobb and South Cobb Government Service Centers take payments too.

Buyers can try the Tax Commissioner's estimator for new home purchasers: enter a fair market value, choose the city or unincorporated tax district and select exemptions. The tool applies the 40% assessed value rule from O.C.G.A. 48-5-7 and covers county taxes only, so a buyer still has to ask the city for its own figure. A seller can run it to show a buyer roughly what the county side of the bill will be.

After the last day for payment, Cobb sends the taxpayer a written notice. If thirty days go by unpaid, a fi. fa. (an execution) can be issued under O.C.G.A. 48-3-3. The debt follows the house, so clear any balance well before closing.

Tax sales run on the first Tuesday of each month in which a sale is planned, held on the Superior Courthouse steps at Flournoy Park in Marietta between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Cobb publishes a Tax Sale Booklet on the process. If you are behind, call 770-528-8600 about payment arrangements before the sale date. Partial payments are accepted, though penalty and interest keep accruing on the balance.

Your deed gets recorded by the Cobb clerk only once the state transfer tax is paid and a PT-61 is on file. The rate works out to $1 on the first $1,000 or any fraction of it, plus 10 cents on each further $100 or fraction of $100. The seller carries the legal liability unless the contract moves it.

Your own homestead exemption ends at the sale, and Cobb asks owners who sold or moved to say so, since staying silent can bring a penalty. The new owner will need the recorded deed to reapply for an exemption of their own.

sections.h2: From signed contract to closing day
sections.html:
With a contract signed, paperwork takes over. The closing attorney or title company pulls the Cobb bill, asks the city for its share and checks that no execution was filed against the parcel. Because the county tax is figured for the full year and follows the property, the settlement statement should show clearly who covers which stretch of the year.

If you are selling to a cash buyer, the same steps apply, only faster, because no lender is waiting on an appraisal. If you appeal a value while a sale is pending, remember that you must still pay at least the appeal amount by the due date.

Before listing, round up the deed, a mortgage payoff figure, current Cobb and city tax bills and permit records for repairs. Check the property search to learn whether the city or the county rules apply. A cash buyer will look at the same papers, though the buyer's price will reflect the house as it stands. A listing buyer's lender will want a clean title and settled tax bills, so clear any balance before an offer comes in. If a tenant lives there, say so up front and plan around the notice the lease requires.

faqs.q: Who covers Cobb property tax when a Marietta house closes?
faqs.a: The contract and settlement statement decide. The Tax Commissioner does not prorate between the parties, and liability generally passes to the purchaser.

faqs.q: What is the payment deadline on a Cobb tax bill?
faqs.a: Bills go out by August 15 and are due October 15. A 5% penalty follows, with interest added monthly. The city bill is separate, so ask Marietta for its date.

faqs.q: Can I get a Marietta building permit online?
faqs.a: Yes. The city takes all permits online, and its Building Inspection Division at 770-794-5659 can answer questions. Code Enforcement at 770-794-5439 handles complaints inside city limits only.

faqs.q: Is every Marietta mailing address inside city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. A Marietta mailing address does not place a property inside the limits. The city's Property Search Tool shows which government's rules apply.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It stops when you sell. Let the Tax Commissioner know you no longer qualify, and expect the buyer to file a new application on their own.
